office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering taxes, school funding, housing rules, health policy and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Two-term Republican incumbent Sam Low, ranking Republican on House Housing, faces Democrat Kathryn Lewandowsky, a registered nurse and first-time candidate. The race contrasts Low's opposition to the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and his supply-side housing record with Lewandowsky's single-payer health care and tenant-protection platform.

candidates.summary: Registered nurse and former hospital union steward running for office for the first time on single-payer health care, housing as a human right and a pause on data-center growth.
highlights: Supports a universal, publicly accountable single-payer health care system; board officer of Whole Washington and One Payer States [S1][S2]
Calls housing a human right and backs tenant protections and more affordable housing [S1][S2]
Says data-center expansion must stop until privacy and cost protections are law [S3]
Endorsed by Snohomish County Democrats and Washington State Stonewall Democrats [S1][S4]

healthcare.basis: Platform calls for a universal single-payer system; she holds board roles in two single-payer advocacy organizations.

housing.basis: Calls housing a human right, not a speculative investment, and supports expanding affordable housing and protecting tenants from predatory practices.

tech.basis: Says data-center growth must stop until laws protect privacy and make corporations bear the costs, and opposes shifting data-center power costs onto families.

climate.basis: Supports accelerating the clean-energy transition and calls climate stability a right; no stated position on carbon pricing.

experience.basis: Has never held public office; running against a two-term incumbent.

social.basis: Endorsed by Washington State Stonewall Democrats; no statement of her own on LGBTQ+ or reproductive policy.

candidates.summary: Two-term Republican incumbent and former Snohomish County councilmember, ranking Republican on House Housing, running on tax relief, transportation, housing supply and public safety.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and joined the 24-hour House floor fight against it [S2][S3][S4]
Says Washington 'does not have a revenue problem. It has a spending problem' [S3]
Prime sponsor of EHB 1345, allowing detached ADUs outside urban growth areas, signed in 2026 [S3][S10]
Voted against 2025 rent-increase limits (EHB 1217) and the clean-fuels expansion (2SHB 1409) [S7][S8]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and ESSB 5814, publicly opposed the income tax and pledges tax relief; multiple independent sources.

spending.basis: Calls the 2026 supplemental budget unsustainable, opposed using pension surplus to ease budget pressure, and says the state has a spending problem.

housing.basis: Blames regulation and permitting for housing costs, sponsored rural ADU legalization, and voted against 2025 rent-increase limits.

climate.basis: Criticizes CCA and fuel taxes as driving costs and wants CCA revenue for roads; voted no on the 2025 clean-fuels expansion.

safety.basis: Lists prioritizing public safety and law-enforcement endorsements; sponsored benefits for families of fallen officers; no detailed enforcement proposals.

experience.basis: Two-term incumbent and committee ranking member, three terms on the county council, 12 bills enacted in 2025-2026.

parental-rights.basis: Voted no on ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.
